main_text.l: of the Flesh. Both these Cases are improved against them, over
whom Satan hath got any advantage of doubting of their Estate.
If they have resisted but ineffectually, or not resisted at all, he char-
geth them with the highest Wilfulnesse, and will so aggravate the
matter that they shall be put in fear, not only that there can be
no Grace (where Sin hath so much power as either to controul so
much light and endeavours,or hath so subjected the Heart to its do-
minion, that it can command without a contradiction) but that
they can have no Hope; that they that sin with so high an hand,
should ever enter into God's Rest. And to this purpose he com-
monly sets before them, that Text of Heb. 10.26. If we sin wil-

main_text.l: maineth no more Sacrifice for sins. Or that of Heb. 6. 4. It is im-

l.i: possible for those who were once enlightned—if they fall away, to

main_text.l: renew them again to Repentance. Both which places speak indeed,
at least, such a difficulty, as in common use of speech, is called
an impossibility, if not an utter absolute impossibility of Repen-
tance and Pardon. But then the sinning wilfully, or falling away,
there mentioned, is only that of Total Apostacy; when Men that
have embraced the Gospel, and by it have met with such impres-
sions of Power, and delight upon their Hearts, which we usually
call Common Grace, do notwithstanding, reject that Gospel as
false and fabulous, and so rise up against it, with Scorn and ut-
most Contempt; as Julian the Apostate did. If now the true
intendment of those Scriptures were considered, by those that
are distressed with them, they might presently see, that they
were put into fear, where no such cause of fear was. But all
Men have not this knowledg, nor do they so duely attend to the
matter of the Apostles Discourse, as to be able to put a right In-
terpretation upon it; upon such Satan imposeth his deceitful
glosses, and tells them: Wilful sinners cannot be restored to Repen-

l.i: tance, but you have sinned wilfully; when sin was before you, you
rushed into it without any consideration; as the Horse into the Battel:
or when God stood in your way with Commands, and advice to the
contrary; when your Consciences warned you not to do so great wicked-
ness, yet you would do it. You were as those that break the Yoke, and

main_text.l: burst the Bonds. Upon this suppofition, that these Texts speak
